newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Santos says keen on WMC oil assets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Santos says keen on WMC oil assets.

text.p: Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd said on Monday it has expressed an interest in acquiring the petroleum assets of WMC Ltd that the mining giant has put up for sale.

Asked if Santos was interested in acquiring the assets, Santos managing director Ross Adler said: "We will certainly have a look at it,...a lot of it is in the USA,...but we will certainly have a look at it."
On August 22, WMC said it would sell its petroleum assets excluding its share of the Goldfields gas transmission pipeline of Western Australia.
Adler made the comment after the company announced a surge in interim net profit to A$88.6 million for the six months to June 30, compared with A$18.5 million for the same 1995 half.
He did not elaborate, but said Santos was not concerned at the rise in its gearing ratio to 54.7 percent at June 30. The ratio has risen from 45.6 percent in first-half 1995.
"We have said over the years we want to maintain no more than 50 percent gearing in the longer term, but we will let it blow out for short periods to finance projects...," Adler said.

He cited an acceleration of exploration projects, the A$200 million development of the Stag joint-venture oil field off Western Australia, and the construction of gas plants in Queensland state to meet demand from Mount Isa base-metals mine owned by MIM Ltd and the Brisbane market.
"We are letting the debt blow out for that. We don't think equity financing is required simply because we have got such strong cash flow.
"I'd say in the next year or two you might see the gearing a bit higher, but...you can bring it back to 50 percent or below fairly quickly."
Net debt rose 24 percent in first-half 1996 to A$846 million and net operating cash flow jumped 17 percent to A$198 million.
